draft.title: Managing water sustainably
card: Managing water sustainably means using it in ways that keep supplies going for the future. It can include reusing water, finding new sources and using less.
used water from showers, baths, washing machines and basins. It can be treated or reused, for example on gardens.
rain that runs off roofs, roads and paths. It can be captured in tanks, ponds or wetlands and used again.
Desalination removes salt from seawater to make fresh water, and it can use a lot of energy. Water trading lets users buy and sell water. Using less, at home or on farms, also makes water last.
draft.remember: Sustainable water use means reusing, capturing, adding to and sharing supplies, and using less.

a.q: A town collects rain running off its roads and car parks into a wetland, then uses it to water parks. Which way of managing water is this?
opts: Harvesting stormwater
Recycling grey water
Desalination
Water trading
a.why: The water is rain runoff from hard surfaces, which is stormwater. Grey water is different because it is used water from household sinks, showers and washing machines.
a.clue: Where did the water come from before it was collected?

b.q: Priya's family in Perth wants to cut the fresh water they use on their garden without buying water from anyone. Which action fits this?
opts: Watering the garden with used shower and laundry water
Buying extra water from a neighbouring farm
Building a plant that removes salt from seawater
Letting the garden take water from the nearest drain
b.why: Reusing grey water gives the garden water that was already used inside the house, so less fresh supply is needed. Buying water is water trading, which moves water between users and does not reduce how much is used.
b.clue: Which choice reuses water the family has already used?

b.best: Watering the garden with used shower and laundry water

problems.detail: The clue 'Which choice reuses water the family has already used?' points straight at the grey water option, so a student can answer without knowing the idea.

'Letting the garden take water from the nearest drain' is vague. A street drain carries stormwater, which the card says can be captured and used, so some students may defend it as stormwater harvesting. It needs a clearer wrong option.

Why (a) says grey water comes from household 'sinks', but the card says 'basins'. In Australia, kitchen sink water is generally not recommended for grey water reuse, so the why should say basins to match the card.

The remember line sorts the methods into five tidy groups: reusing, capturing, adding to, sharing and using less. The card frames them as three: reusing, finding new sources and using less. 'Adding to' and 'sharing' are labels the card never uses.

b.q: Priya's family in Perth wants to water their garden with grey water. Which action does this?
